correctness.rationale: The compactly supported hyperbolic cardinal basis yields a positive tridiagonal Gram symbol A+2B cosω with A>2B. Its explicitly invertible geometric Green matrix supplies the exact kernel; absolute values of its sections are strictly convex between knots, forcing nodal maximizers. One sign change in each half-line cell gives an evaluated elementary integral, yielding the sharp endpoint formula. Independently derived uniform expansions of the Gram entries and signed-cell integral give 2+θ²/120+O(θ⁴); large tension gives A~1/θ, q→0, J~1/θ and limit 2. The 34 finite-section consistency assertions are auxiliary only.

originality.rationale: The claimed invariant is the exact sharp L1/L∞ operator norm of a specific orthogonal cardinal exponential-spline projector, including knot-location rigidity and nonmonotone tension response. Kayumov supplies sharp worst-mesh bounds rather than this curve; Unser--Blu supply a general projection representation but not the endpoint maximization in inspected passages; Chebyshev work gives nonsharp boundedness; interpolation constants are for another operator. Searches of published mathematical records and the available prior-claims database found no stronger matching result. Priority is best-knowledge only, with explicitly substantial full-text access risks.

value.rationale: The cardinal exponential-spline projection norm is a natural stability constant of least-squares approximation, rather than an arbitrary slice. Known worst-mesh constant 3 misses its exact uniform-mesh dependence. The result proves a genuine, finite-tension amplification (quadratic excess 1/120) followed by recovery to baseline, and locates every worst-case spatial point at a knot; these quantitative stability properties matter when selecting spline tension.
